annotations.text:
F · SANCTUARY  ← my recommendation
Warm limestone ground, deep liturgical green, Instrument Serif headings over Manrope UI. Soft 12px radii, warm hairline borders, no shadows.

Why: it is the only direction here whose palette isn't tech-blue or grey — it reads as the Augustine Institute rather than a generic SaaS dashboard, and the serif gives the numbers real authority. Colour appears only where it means something: green for committed and on-track, burgundy for needs-attention.

Tradeoff: warm palettes date faster than neutral ones, and the serif needs care at small sizes on Windows machines.

G · ATLAS
Navy rail with a copper accent, Space Grotesk over IBM Plex Sans, 6px radii, cards with a 2px top accent bar, sticky page header with section tabs.

Why: the strongest navigational structure of the three. The persistent rail plus per-page tabs makes it obvious where you are in an app with three real sections, and the copper is distinctive without being loud.

Tradeoff: the rail costs 236px of horizontal room on every screen, and the navy is heavy enough that the app feels more corporate than the other two.

H · GRAPHITE
Near-monochrome. One typeface (Instrument Sans), hairline rules instead of cards, 4px radii, and a single amber reserved entirely for needs-attention. Hierarchy comes from weight, size and space — not colour.

Why: the most restrained and the most 'expensive' looking. Nothing decorative survives, so the data is the only thing on screen. It will also still look right in five years.

Tradeoff: austere. Status is carried by outlined chips rather than colour, so scanning the queue for blocked items is slower than in F or G.

ALL FOUR PAGES, ALL THREE DIRECTIONS — use the pages menu in the toolbar to switch between F, G, H and the earlier five.

Nothing was dropped. Every control from the live app is here: fiscal-year editing, add/edit content, budget sources, needs attention, collaborators, quarter expansion, ClickUp push, manage key, 6/9/12-month views, backlog, ongoing series, Focus Five, drag-to-reorder, group/sort toggles, the full review detail panel with notes toolbar and update log, delete and save.

Figures and titles are your real demo data. Static mockups — nothing clicks.

THE EARLIER FIVE, kept so nothing is lost. Dashboard only.

You said C · Brief and D · Vault were fine but not exciting — F, G and H are the follow-up. Sanctuary takes Brief's calm and gives it a palette with some conviction; Graphite pushes Brief's restraint much further; Atlas answers Vault's structure without the dark ground.
